items.title: Place walls as whole squares with an unambiguous footprint and height
items.body:
The owner supplied a current screenshot on 2026-09-27 and explicitly chose a different interaction: place walls as **whole grid squares**, with a clear distinction between the occupied ground footprint and the wall's visible height. The current edge-based selection still fails that expectation (see #886).

Observed: a rectangular drag paints thin boundary strips; after completion, the walls read as taller blocks, so the player cannot tell which square is occupied. The existing hover ghost matches the edge data, but the representation itself remains ambiguous.

Acceptance:
- A wall placement gesture targets full, visibly highlighted squares. The committed wall occupies the same squares the preview marked; no edge inference changes the result.
- A top-down footprint stays visible even where the vertical face, cap, or neighboring wall art overlaps it. Door placement and room enclosure remain coherent.
- Existing edge-wall saves load through an explicit versioned compatibility path; construction, pathfinding, topology, undo, removal, and costs use one consistent geometry rule.
- Browser playtest: draw a four-sided 4×4 cell, inspect hover and completed footprint at normal zoom and 1920×1080, add a door, designate a Cell, save/reload, then remove one wall. Every occupied square and open passage must match what the player saw before committing.

The owner also requested room templates; track that independently because it can reuse the finished placement geometry.

items.title: [RETRACTED] The game explains why zoning failed, in a box that is 0 pixels tall — and nothing points at it
items.body:
Found by a **mouse-only** playtest of the route a new player actually walks — no keyboard shortcuts — on `main` at `6c309fc` (v0.0.200), Chromium at 1440×900, driving the real page (`index.html` + `src/main.ts`).

This is the strongest candidate yet for the owner's original complaint: *"nie mogłem postawić więzienia … grając sam"*.

## What happens

Rooms → Cell → "Draw on map" → drag a 4×4 → the button reads **"Designate 4 × 4"** and is live. Pressing it sends:

```json
{"type":"ZoneRoom","roomId":"room.cell","x":17,"y":17,"width":4,"height":4}
```

and the worker answers:

```json
{"refusal":{"sequence":14,"tick":0,"reason":"zone.not-enclosed"}}
```

`ROOMS` stays `0`. Every later `PlaceObject` is then refused `place-object.outside-room`. **Nothing on screen changes at any point.**

The explanation *is* produced, and it is correct:

```json
[{"id":"refusal-14",
  "text":"The room was not zoned — this room type must be enclosed, and the area you drew is open on at least one side.Warning",
  "boxWidth":0,"boxHeight":0}]
```

## Why, in three lines that are each defensible alone

| line | what it does |
| --- | --- |
| `src/ui/hud/hud-state.ts:51-54` | `collapsedPanels: ['alerts']` — Alerts start folded, deliberately: *"The HUD frames the world and must not cover it; a list that is empty most of the time should not hold open a rectangle over the prison to say so."* |
| `src/ui/hud/hud.ts:1239-1248` | that section is built with **no `trailing`** badge, so the folded header carries no count |
| `src/ui/hud/hud.ts:1244` | the only `set-panel-collapsed` for `'alerts'` anywhere in `src/` is the header's own toggle — **nothing ever un-folds it** |

Measured on arrival: `{"headerText":"ALERTS","ariaExpanded":"false","sectionCollapsed":"true","childElementCount":2}`.

**The Build panel already solves this and is the contrast that makes it a defect rather than a taste question.** Its queue section is *also* collapsed when it appears — and passes `trailing: queueCount` (`src/ui/hud/build-panel.ts:1522-1528`), with its own comment saying why: *"a queue then costs this panel a header and a count, and costs it a list only when the player asks for one."* So the folded queue header still reads "1 waiting · 0 being built". The folded Alerts header reads nothing.

**Consequence:** all **40** reasons in `REFUSAL_LABEL_KEYS` (`src/ui/simulation-alerts.ts:33-73`) are dark by default. Not one of them can reach a player who has not thought to expand a section that never asks to be expanded.

## What was checked and withdrawn

**The live "Designate" button is not the defect.** It is deliberate and reasoned at `src/ui/hud/rooms-panel.ts:1164-1190` (#493/#498): `classifyArea` can be stale, so the panel warns — and it *did*, showing `"OPEN ON AT LEAST ONE SIDE"` — and lets the simulation decide. That reasoning ends *"the real simulation still decides"*. **And the decision is delivered through the 0×0 box.** Two defensible decisions composing into a dead end, which is why neither file looks wrong on its own.

## A second, smaller edge in the same place

A Cell prints one block — `"NEEDS AT LEAST 2 × 3 TILES / MUST BE ENCLOSED / NEEDS 1 × BED / NEEDS 1 × TOILET"` — and the four lines behave three different ways: too-small **disables** Designate (`rooms-panel.ts:1567`), not-enclosed leaves it live and refuses silently, and bed and toilet are post-conditions. **Two of the four teach the player "you can add it later"**, which is exactly the wrong lesson to carry into the enclosure line.

## The informed route does work

Buy bricks → fast-forward → four wall runs → *then* zone: `"rooms":1`, `"zoning":{…,"enclosure":"sealed"}`. **The game is finishable; the ordering is the entire difficulty, and nothing states it.**

## Also settled by the same pass, recorded so nobody re-derives it

- **Camera calibration corrected.** Tile (0,0)'s top-left is at **(−304, −574)** at 1440×900, 64 px/tile. The rule is `(viewportW/2 − 1024, viewportH/2 − 1024)` — the camera is centred on world (1024,1024), the *corner* of `NEW_PRISON_ORIGIN_TILE`. The previously recorded `(−224, −512)` is that same rule evaluated at 1600×1024, so it was never wrong, only unlabelled.
- **Save → reload → load of a mouse-built prison loses nothing measurable.** 1 ROOMS, 22,600 FUNDS, day 2 on both sides; the room returns with *"Cell at 12, 12 is missing 1 × Bed"*; the queue returns. Only the Rooms panel's *selection* resets to "Staff Room".
- **Doors and walls reach the worker correctly.** A south-edge drag arrives as `y:16, edge:"north"`; a door as `{"definitionId":"door-wooden","x":12,"y":16,"edge":"north"}`.
- **Touch and pinch: an empty category, with the numbers that establish it.** Tap places on the nearest edge; a two-finger pinch-out zooms (the same screen point resolves `y:13` → `y:15`, ≈3×) and emits **0** stray commands; a one-finger drag lays a run exactly as the hint promises.
- **`object.sink`'s absence is deliberate**, documented at `src/simulation/construction/definition.ts:330`. Not a defect.

## Observations whose cause is *not* established

Stated separately on purpose — these are measurements, not diagnoses.

- **Refusal is a latch.** `state-machine.ts:517` republishes `refusals.last` with every counts message, so at tick 2,334 the payload still carried a `tick:0` refusal. The design is deliberate; whether a stale, undated warning is the right thing to keep showing is a product question, not a bug report.
- One `World renderer: TypeError: Failed to fetch` at `atlas-library.ts:19` during a `reload()` under a 2× clock. **Did not reproduce** across three plain reloads, and `/assets/actors/asset-registry.json` returned `{"ok":true,"status":200}` from the reloaded page each time. Most likely the outgoing page's aborted fetch — **not established**.

## Not reached

Any prison larger than one cell; guards or prisoners in a mouse-built prison; the Security and Regime tabs; the Overview tab beyond its arrival text; viewports other than 1440×900; the Import/Export path.

## The weakest claim, and what would change it

**That the folded Alerts box is *why* the owner could not build a prison.** What was measured is that the explanation renders at 0×0 and that nothing points at it. Nobody observed the owner's session. What would settle it: the owner saying they had Alerts open, or a second player getting past the zone step unaided with it still folded — either moves this from *"this is the wall"* to *"this is a wall"*.

| 2,399 | day about to end | 24,935 | 300 | 1 | 1 | 1 | `completed` | 1 / 1 | `['sleep-surface']` | `completed` | `action.sleep` |
| **2,400** | **the state pays** | **25,235** | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | `completed` | 1 / 1 | `['sleep-surface']` | `completed` | `action.sleep` |
| 4,800 | second day paid | **25,535** | 0 | 1 | 1 | 1 | `completed` | 1 / 1 | `['sleep-surface']` | `completed` | `action.sleep` |

`accommodationBacklogTicks` is **0** at every row, `completedCount` is 1 from
tick 200 and `failedCount` never leaves 0. Needs at tick 400, of 255:
`sleep 254.7`, `safety 254.9`, `hygiene 250`, `hunger 242.5`, `bladder 235`,
`recreation 251.3` — sleep is the one that stays pinned at the top while
everything else falls, which is the bed doing work rather than a coincidence.

### The three figures the brief asked to re-verify

- **A zoned cell registering `capacity: 0` with no capabilities, so
  `findAvailable` returns nothing.** Still exactly true at tick 2 — and no
  longer permanent. It is now the state of a room with nothing in it, and the
  player leaves it by placing something.
- **An admitted prisoner sitting in `accommodation-assignment` with a rising
  backlog.** Not any more, when there is a bed: the arrival reaches `completed`
  between tick 151 and tick 200 with `accommodationBacklogTicks` never leaving
  0. With no bed it still waits, and that path is still pinned by
  `prisoner-admission-loop.test.ts`.
- **The income line paying 300 × 0.** It pays 300 × 1. **The treasury moves
  upward for the first time from something other than spending:** 24,935 →
  25,235 at tick 2,400, and → 25,535 at 4,800. Every previous session could
  only ever spend (`ProcurementSystem.cancel`'s refund aside).

`tests/integration/object-placement-loop.test.ts` drives all of it, plus the
save round trip and the undo.

## What a player actually sees after this, precisely

- The Build panel has a third row, **Bed**, between *Brick Wall* and *Wooden
  Door* — `CATEGORY_RANK` already ranked `object` second, so the position was
  content's choice and not this change's. It is labelled by `object.bed`'s own
  `nameKey`, so no new locale key was authored.
- Selecting it and pressing *Start placing* arms a **different tool**: the world
  pointer draws a 1×2 footprint rectangle at the hovered tile, and one press
  places one bed. Selecting a wall row again arms the wall tool. The panel's
  numeric coordinate fields also work, so the placement has a keyboard route on
  the day it ships.
- The bed waits for a plank (≈100 ticks after a purchase, 5 s at 1×) and then
  builds (≈60 ticks, 3 s), drawing as a planned ghost and then as a solid
  object at its real 1×2 size.
- The status strip's `Rooms` block stops reading `1 room, 0 of 0 occupied` and
  starts reading `0 of 1`, then `1 of 1` once somebody lives there.
- An `Admit prisoner` press is accepted and **completes**. The prisoner walks to
  the cell and sleeps; `action.sleep`, `action.use-toilet` and
  `action.eat-in-cell` all become reachable, because `own-accommodation`
  re-checks neither gate.
- The treasury rises by 300 a day per occupied place.
- **The caveat, unpapered:** the Rooms panel still reports the cell's *toilet*
  requirement as unmet, because the catalogue's `room.cell` requires
  `object.toilet` and no buildable places one. So the milestone the ADR names is
  phase 2, and what this ships is a cell that works and reads as unfinished.
  `action.shower`, `action.eat-meal`, `action.yard-recreation`,
  `action.common-room-recreation` and `action.classroom-education` are all still
  unreachable: the rooms they name still contain nothing.
- A misplaced bed can be taken back with `Undo` (the object leaves the world with
  its order) but there is no *remove* control — that is phase 3.

## What ADR 0028 got wrong about the code

Three corrections, all in the same direction — the tree moved between v0.0.45,
which the ADR was written against, and v0.0.56.

1. **`door-wooden` is not fixed by phase 1, and cannot be.** The ADR says phase
   1 "also fixes a shipped defect: `door-wooden` stops being a catalogue row
   that consumes a plank and does nothing." It does not. A placed object names an
   id in `src/content/object-catalog.ts` and that catalogue declares no wooden
   door — `object.loading-dock-door` is a three-tile delivery door with a
   `'delivery-access'` capability. A door's own state lives in `DoorRegistry`,
   and connecting a completed order to it is navigation work with consequences
   for `TopologyManager`. `door-wooden` is left exactly as found, with no
   `placesObjectId`, and the defect is still open. The reason is recorded at
   `edgeNumericIdFor`.
2. **Most of the renderer work the ADR budgeted for was already done.** Decision
   5 and ADR 0022 §4 say "no area preview or selection rectangle exists anywhere
   in the tree", that `BuildOverlay`'s signature is not reusable, and that
   `BuildToolPort` "carries no shape". Two of those three stopped being true when
   the Rooms tab shipped: `AreaOverlay` already draws a tile rectangle with a
   per-tile hairline, `TileRect`/`pickTileAtWorld` already live in
   `area-picking.ts`, and `RoomToolPort` is already the second-port precedent
   the ADR argues for. What was actually left was one interface, one preview
   call and the three-way arming arbitration.
3. **The objects section sits inside `simulation`, not beside it.** Decision 6
   says "a new optional payload section". It is one — but nested next to
   `economy` rather than next to `identity`, because `economy` is the precedent
   for an optional subsystem section added inside `simulation` with no bump of
   its own, and because the restore *ordering* constraint decision 6 names
   (objects and bounds in place before the first `findAvailable*`) is satisfied
   for free there: `restoreSessionSystems` registers instances and places
   objects in step 2, before prisoner state arrives in step 3.

And one decision the ADR deliberately left open that this had to take:
**`outside-room` is a refusal.** Open question 5 says decision 1 permits an
object outside a room structurally and leaves the gesture question open, with
`door-wooden` as the case for permitting it. `PlaceObject` refuses it, because
capacity is derived per room instance so a bed in a field is a plank spent on a
row nothing reads — and `door-wooden` is untouched, because a door is not placed
through this command. The reasoning is at `ObjectPlacementService` so it can be
overruled without reading a diff.

**One thing deliberately not shipped:** rotation. `PlacedObject.orientation` and
the save carry the full `0..3` range and `orientedFootprint` is implemented and
tested, but nothing produces anything but `0` — decision 5's rotate key needs an
`ACTION_IDS` member, a default binding and a description key, and a command field
no producer sets would be exactly the dead vocabulary
`unconsumed-command-contract` exists to catch. It arrives with the control, with
no save move.

## The V5 migration, and how the premise was verified

V5 does three things and only one of them needed a bump:

- `simulation.objects` is **new and optional**. Absence means "no object has
  been placed", which is what every V4 build meant because no V4 build could
  place one — the optional-field pattern exactly, so the migration adds no
  section.
- A room instance gains optional **`width`/`height`**. Optional at V5 because a
  V4 row genuinely does not record the rectangle and there is no honest default;
  an instance with no rectangle is attributed no objects, so its capacity stays
  0, which is its pre-object-placement behaviour.
- A room instance **loses `capacity` and `objectCapabilities`**. `capacity` was
  *required*, so removing it changes the shape. That is the bump.

**The premise is measured, not cited.** The migration is lossless because
`RoomZoningService` is the only thing in `src/` that has ever registered an
instance and it registered `capacity: 0` with `objectCapabilities: []`
unconditionally. That was re-verified on this branch before anything relied on
it — it is still true at `zoning.ts` — and
`tests/migrations/save-v4-to-v5.test.ts`'s first case reads the two fields off
the real `ZoneRoom` command path, so a future change that authored a capacity
fails that test instead of quietly migrating a value it had assumed away. The
same file proves the other half: a migrated row restores to exactly the values
that were dropped.

Both checked-in V1 fixtures are unchanged and now walk V1→V2→V3→V4→V5.
`supabase/migrations/` is untouched.

## Red-proofs

Each was made red by reverting the one change it is about, then reapplied.

| Reverted | What went red |
| --- | --- |
| `finalizeConstruction` stops calling `onOrderCompleted` | **10 of the 14** cases in `object-placement-loop.test.ts`, including the capacity, the status strip, the housing, the sleep, the save round trip and the determinism pair. Restored: 14 passed. |
| `unzone`'s occupancy check | *leaves no dangling occupant when the room a bed stands in is un-zoned* — 1 failed, 13 passed. Restored: 14 passed. |
| `PlacedObjectRegistry.all()` returns insertion order | *sorts by (y, x) and never by placedObjectId*, **and both cases of `canonical-iteration-contract`** — 3 failed of 36. Restored: 36 passed. |
| the V4 → V5 migration carries `capacity` through | *drops the two derived fields*, *decodes a real V4 save through the whole chain* and *rejects a corrupt V4 save* — 3 failed of 9. Restored: 9 passed. |
| the tile-index / in-flight check in `place` | *refuses a tile another object already covers* and *refuses a tile claimed by an order still in flight* — 2 failed. Restored: 14 passed. |
| the containment check in `place` | *refuses a tile in no room* — 1 failed. Restored: 14 passed. |

The third row is worth a note: reverting the sort failed
`canonical-iteration-contract` as well as the unit case, so the ordering rule is
guarded by a structural gate and by an assertion about the answer rather than by
either alone.

The fourth row is the one that changed the change. Reverting the migration
failed only two of the three cases at first, because neither read the payload
through the *strict* V5 schema the chain validates against — so a third case was
added (`decodes a real V4 save with a room in it through the whole chain`, its
own commit) and the revert then failed all three. That is the red-proof finding
a hole in the test rather than confirming one.

## Verification

- `npx tsc -b --pretty false` — clean.
- `npx vitest run` — `Test Files 195 passed (195)`, `Tests 2169 passed | 1 skipped (2170)`.
- `npx vite build` — clean.
- browser suite (`playwright test --config tests/browser/playwright.config.ts`,
  `LOCKSTATE_BROWSER_TEST_PORT=5241`) — **147 passed, 1 failed in 4.8m**. The one
  failure is the Git-LFS atlas decode case
  (`/assets/actors/actor.cook.base.idle.png did not decode at its authored
  size`), which is the expected local failure: the atlas PNGs are 131-byte LFS
  pointers in this checkout and CI has the real bytes. No other case failed.

Do not merge — ADR 0028's status is being changed on a separate branch and this
touches no ADR status line or `STATUS-QUEUE.md` entry.

items.title: Finish the `expect(x.ok).toBe(true)` sweep — twelve result types read, twelve made to refuse
items.body:
## What this finishes [#1081](https://github.com/woogitsu/lockstate/pull/1081) converted 75 of 121 `expect(.ok).toBe(true)` sites — the persistence and session family, the one whose false arm is a `SaveWriteError` — and counted 46 left, five of them in the blocked `browser` job. This is the other **41**, plus **7** of a second spelling that PR's grep could not match. ## The counts, re-measured rather than taken on trust The brief for this pass came with a warning that its own figures had been wrong repeatedly. They are not. On `fece2499`: ``` $ grep -rn '\.ok)\.toBe(true)' tests/ | wc -l 47 $ grep -rn '\.ok)\.toBe(true)' tests/helpers/expect-ok.ts | wc -l # the pattern quoted in its own docblock 1 ``` 46 real sites, and #1081's per-family breakdown is right to the site: navigation 11 (9 unit, 2 determinism), construction 11, operations 6, `local-save-*` 5, input 2, foundation 2, restored-scope 2, economy 2, services 2, security 1, procurement 1, rendered-art contract 1. **Nothing to correct.** The five in `tests/browser/local-save-*.spec.ts` are untouched — they belong to the `browser` job, blocked on the runner pool ([#1008](https://github.com/woogitsu/lockstate/issues/1008)) — and `tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts` was held by another agent while this ran. ## The judgement call, and it went the other way from expectation `expectOk` is worth only what the false arm carries, so each type was read at its declaration and then **made to refuse**, by driving the real production function and recording the received value. The expectation going in was that some of these types would be a bare `{ ok: false }` and should be left alone. **None is.** | type | what its false arm carries | sites | | --- | --- | --- | | `RouteResult` (`route.ts:31`) | `failure.reason` of four, plus `blockedBy: { doorId, reason }` | 15 | | `InventoryResult` (`inventory.ts:8`) | `error.kind`, `itemId`, `available`/`reserved`, `requested` | 9 | | `SaveDecodeResult` (`save-schema.ts:1535`) | `error.code`, `error.message`, `atVersion` | 6 | | `PurchaseOutcome` (`procurement.ts:98`) | `reason` of four | 4 | | `BrowserSuiteSelectionResult` (`browser-suites.ts:90`) | `error`, naming the unknown suite and the known ones | 4 | | `InputSettingsValidationResult` (`settings.ts:11`) | `reason` of two, plus `conflicts[]` | 2 | | `SaveResult` (`repository.ts:16`) | `error.code`, `error.message` | 2 | | `ProtocolDecodeResult` (`decode.ts:52`) | `error.code`, `message`, `issues[]` | 1 | | `LoadedCatalogResult` (`catalog.ts:99`) | `locale`, `message` | 1 | | `ChallengeDefinitionAuthenticationResult` (`challenge.ts:138`) | `code`, `message` | 1 | | aspect check (`validate-rendered-art-catalog.d.mts:18`) | `reason`, a sentence carrying the arithmetic | 1 | | `PurchaseCancelOutcome` (`procurement.ts:127`) | `reason`, and the union has exactly one member | 1 | **The last row is the weak one, converted anyway with the reason stated rather than buried.** `PurchaseCancelRefusalReason` is `'not-pending'` and nothing else, deliberately: `procurement.ts:101-110` records that this system cannot tell an id it has never seen from a delivery that has already landed, and that a second reason would be it claiming to know which. So the printed `{ ok: false, reason: 'not-pending' }` states a fact but discriminates nothing. What that one site gains is the **label**, naming which of the test's two orders failed to cancel — a smaller win than the other eleven, and it should not be read as one. ## The class this sweep is really about `expect(.ok, ).toBe(true)` is the same defect wearing a label, and `.ok).toBe(true)` cannot match it. There are **21** (19 `true`, 2 `false`). Ten of the nineteen already hand-roll the reason out of the result: ```ts expect(decoded.ok, decoded.ok ? '' : decoded.error.message).toBe(true); expect(accepted.ok, accepted.ok ? '' : JSON.stringify(accepted.error)).toBe(true); ``` `expectOk`, written by hand, ten times, in six files, in three spellings, by people who each wanted exactly this and had nowhere to get it. **That is a better argument for the helper than the single CI red that prompted it.** Seven of the nineteen sit in files this commit was already editing and are converted with them — leaving two spellings of one assertion three lines apart in the same file is worse than either. **The other twelve are left and named**, so the next pass does not re-find them: `simulation-worker-protocol.test.ts:564,572,578`, `worker-projection-channel.test.ts:186`, `command-success-notices.test.ts:290`, `worker-status-counts.test.ts:396,615,955`, `worker-state-machine.test.ts:339`, `worker-render-delta.test.ts:223,353`, and `hud-zoom-control.spec.ts:96` (`tests/browser/`, not ours). They are the worker-protocol surface, and the hand-rolled ones already print their reason, so what they would gain is consistency and narrowing rather than evidence. That is a smaller change and belongs in its own. ## Proved in place, not only in a harness Two sites were watched going red with production code mutated, so the pair is the **same line** before and after under the **same** mutation. `Container.reserve` under-reporting available stock by one (`inventory.ts:48`), at `tests/unit/operations-inventory.test.ts:33`: | | message | | --- | --- | | before | `AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality` | | after | `AssertionError: the first claim, on all five bricks did not succeed: expected { ok: false, error: { …(4) } } to be undefined`
`+ Received: { "error": { "available": 4, "itemId": "item.brick", "kind": "insufficient-stock", "requested": 5 }, "ok": false }` | `canAccessDoor`'s clearance test shifted by `+ 100` (`route-context.ts:28`), at `tests/unit/navigation-router.test.ts:22`: | | message | | --- | --- | | before | `AssertionError: expected false to be true // Object.is equality` | | after | `AssertionError: the cleared route through the gated door did not succeed: expected { ok: false, failure: { …(2) } } to be undefined`
`+ Received: { "failure": { "blockedBy": { "doorId": "door-medical", "reason": "insufficient-clearance" }, "reason": "permission-denied" } }` | The other ten types were made to refuse the same way — real production functions, in a throwaway harness rather than in `tests/`. Three whose received value is worth quoting: ``` BrowserSuiteSelectionResult: { "ok": false, "error": "no browser suite is called \"artefact\". Known suites: browser, artifact." } LoadedCatalogResult: { "ok": false, "locale": "pt-BR", "message": "network down" } aspect: { "ok": false, "reason": "pixel size 1790x1280 does not exactly reproduce the footprint aspect 1.4x1 (cross-multiplied against a denominator of 20: 35840 != 35800)" } ``` ## Three places this removed an assertion rather than replacing one - `economy-negative-balance-readers.test.ts:149-150` held `expect(decoded.ok ? null : decoded.error.code).toBe(null)` **and** `expect(decoded.ok).toBe(true)` on consecutive lines. One `expectOk` has the identical pass condition and prints the whole error rather than its `code`. - `navigation-shared-plan-equivalence.test.ts:131` was `expect(throughB.ok && throughC.ok).toBe(true)`, which could not say which of the two failed. Two calls now can. - `navigation-flat-search-reference.test.ts:30,35` were `expect(guardRoute.ok && guardRoute.route.totalCost).toBe(guardFlatCost)` — a boolean smuggled into a cost comparison to satisfy the compiler. Narrowing removes the `ok &&`. Ten `if (!x.ok) return;` / `{ continue; }` guards that existed only for the compiler go the same way. ## The one `!` this needed `findRouteUsingFlowField` answers `RouteResult | undefined` (`flow-field.ts:138`), so `navigation-flow-field.test.ts:32` cannot reach `expectOk` without a non-null assertion. The line above already asserts definedness, the `!` is about *that* and not about `ok`, and it buys the deletion of an `if (viaField?.ok) { … }` wrapper whose false arm silently skipped the cost comparison the loop exists to make. The helper's docblock argues against `!` for narrowing `ok`; this is not that. **If a reviewer would rather have the guard back than the `!`, say so and it goes back** — it is the one line here I would defend least. ## Labels Noun phrases naming the precondition, each read against the code that produces it: `'the walk in through the gap the undo left'`, `"the carry job's claim on four of the six on the shelf"`, `'the round-tripped envelope whose buffer carries no gesture id'`. The two mistakes #1081 recorded were checked for by name. No label repeats the argument list the reader is already looking at. Every numeral was read off the call it describes rather than off its last argument — `purchase(orderId, itemId, quantity, tick, spendClass)` puts the quantity third, so `'the ten further bricks put on the road'` is the `10` of `purchase('jit:probe', BRICK, 10, 0, 'construction')` and not its tick. Apostrophes are inside double-quoted strings. Every import was opened and read rather than appended by a "last line starting with `import`" heuristic: three of these files (`input`, `browser-suite-selection`, `construction-geometry`) end their import block with a multi-line form, which is exactly what broke a file in the first pass. ## An observation, not acted on `tests/unit/navigation-work-budget-and-cache.test.ts:30-36` is titled *"does not mutate the caller-supplied stats object when no stats are passed (opt-in, zero overhead)"*, and its body passes no stats object and asserts only that the route succeeded. **Nothing in it could fail if the property in its title were violated.** Converting the assertion does not fix that, and inventing the missing one is a separate decision about what the test should require, so it is recorded rather than guessed at. ## What this does not claim Nothing here changes a pass condition, so **no gate got stronger.** Every one of these 48 sites still passes for exactly the inputs it passed for before; the only change is what the log holds when one stops passing. Whether that ever pays is unfalsifiable until one of them goes red — which is the same weakest claim #1081 named, and the same answer: a reproduction would settle it. The narrower claim I would defend is the twelve-row table above, and it is measured rather than reasoned: every false arm was produced by real production code and its value recorded. ## Gates | gate | result | | --- | --- | | `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` | clean | | `tsc -b` and `tsc -b tsconfig.tools.json` | clean | | `vitest run` on this branch | **417 files, 4895 passed \| 3 skipped** | | `vitest run` on `origin/main` at `fece2499` | **417 files, 4895 passed \| 3 skipped** | The baseline was measured here in a second worktree rather than taken from the brief. `tests/perf/` is untouched by this commit, so the opt-in measurement harness #1081 had to run does not apply — and the side finding it recorded still stands: nothing in `package.json` or `ci.yml` invokes that config. The `browser` job is expected to be `cancelled` at its 30-minute budget, as on every open PR right now (`#1008`); nothing here touches it, and the five `local-save-*` sites inside it are deliberately left. --- 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01KKu9oyVgb8WKeQPVAcX4hc --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_01KKu9oyVgb8WKeQPVAcX4hc)_

items.title: [Audit] What a player can actually do: one of thirteen systems does observable work, and the shortest path to a loop
items.body:
An end-to-end reachability audit traced from the real composition root (`src/main.ts`) outward, not from the tests. **This question is not answered anywhere else in the repository**, and the answer is short.

Claims are **VERIFIED** (read and/or executed) or **INFERRED**. Executed claims were driven through `createNewSimulationRuntime` and `Kernel.step()` — the same runtime the worker builds — from throwaway scripts outside the repository. Raw output is quoted.

---

## 1. What a player can do today

1. **Load the page and look at an empty grey world.** The worker is `uninitialized`; the strip reads `Day --` and zeros.
2. **Press "New prison".** The only thing on the page that starts a simulation. You get a 32×32 square of dirt with one owned chunk, and a save.
3. **Look at the prison.** Pan with the middle button, WASD or arrows; zoom with wheel, `+`, `−`; one-finger drag and two-finger pinch on touch. **Nothing the camera does reaches the simulation.**
4. **Start and stop time.** Pause / Play / Fast-forward genuinely work. One in-game day is two minutes of real time at ×1.
5. **Switch to Build and choose "Brick wall" or "Wooden door".** The only two entries.
6. **Press "Place on map", then click or drag along a tile edge.** A translucent brown box appears. It is a build *order*.
7. **Watch that box stay translucent forever.** It never becomes a wall — there is no way in the entire interface to buy the bricks it waits for. It survives every save and reload.
8. **Type coordinates instead.** Same outcome. **A coordinate outside the owned chunk is silently discarded** — nothing appears and nothing says why.
9. **Save, load, delete, export.** All work. Export downloads a file the application cannot import back.
10. **`?actors=demo`** shows three scripted sprites walking in a circle. A rendering demonstration, not simulation state.

**That is the complete list.** The single mechanical consequence a player can produce is item 6: a ghost outline.

---

## 2. The proof, executed

`createNewSimulationRuntime(0)`, one `PlaceBuildOrder` exactly as `main.ts` builds it at tile (16,16), then 2,000 ticks — 100 in-game seconds:

```
[A] after 2000 ticks state=materials-pending progress=0 failReason=undefined
[A] treasury=25000
[A] chunk topEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

`[[0,1024]]` is 1,024 run-length-encoded zeroes: **no wall anywhere in the world.**

The same runtime with one `PurchaseMaterials` command inserted first:

```
[B] state=completed treasury=24600
[B] chunk topEdge=[[0,528],[1,1],[0,495]]
```

Index 528 = `16 × 32 + 16` — the exact tile. **The construction pipeline is complete and correct; the only missing link in the whole chain is a producer for one command.**

---

## 3. Thirteen systems run every tick. One does work a player can see.

Read from a live runtime's `systemExecutionOrder`:

| System | Iterates | Non-empty in a reachable session? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prisoners.intake` | live prisoner entities | **No** — `admitPrisoner` has no caller in `src/` |
| `prisoners.needs-decay` | same | **No** (see #259) |
| **`construction`** | `orderedOrders()` | **Yes — the one reachable system.** Stalls at `materials-pending` |
| `procurement` | `this.pending` | **No** — returns on line 156 every tick, 20 times a second, forever |
| `navigation` | graph + queue | **Partially.** `ensureGraph()` does real work; **nothing reads its output** — no route is ever requested |
| `prisoners.actions` | prisoner query | No |
| `operations.jobs` | `activeJobs()` | **No** — `submitCarryItem` has no caller |
| `contraband.intelligence` | decays an empty ledger | No |
| `security.deployment` | `allGuardIds()` | **No** — `GuardRoster.hire` has no caller |
| `security.patrol` | same | No |
| `incidents.trigger` | `sectorIds` (empty) | No |
| `contraband.search` | queued orders (none) | No |
| `incidents.response` | `openIncidents()` | No |

**Eleven of thirteen iterate permanently empty collections.** One more does real computation nothing reads.

### Three subsystems are not even registered

- **`TopologyManager`** (229 lines) is constructed, exposed on `SimulationRuntime.topology`, and **`update()` is never called anywhere in `src/`**. It has no `id`/`order`/`schedule`, **so it cannot be registered with the kernel at all.** Room enclosure detection never runs.
- **`UtilityNetwork`** — two instances built, no `update`, and `addNode`/`connect`/`evaluate` have no caller outside their own module.
- **`ContainerRegistry`, `JobBoard`, `JobWorkerPool`** — built empty; only the construction container is registered and nothing is ever put in it.

---

## 4. Three findings worth their own attention

### A finished wooden door writes nothing and creates no door

`edgeNumericIdFor` returns `0` for `category: 'object'`, so `finalizeConstruction` only bumps the geometry revision. Executed:

```
[C] door state=completed
[C] topEdge=[[0,1024]]  leftEdge=[[0,1024]]
```

It exists only as a 0.55-tile-high brown slab drawn from the order list. `DoorRegistry.register` is called from exactly one place — restoring from a snapshot. **Nothing creates the first door.**

### A refused order gives the player no feedback of any kind

The command reply acknowledges *receipt*, not effect: `state-machine.ts:524-535` posts `status: 'queued'` as soon as the kernel accepts it. A `failReason` of `out-of-bounds` or `unowned-land` is mapped to `undefined` by `phaseOf` and drawn as nothing. Executed, typing `100, 100` into fields that have no `min`/`max`:

```
[E] far order state=failed failReason=out-of-bounds
```

The refusal line stays hidden because the command *was* queued successfully, and no ghost appears. (`x = 2e9`, `x = -5`, `x = 9e12` all fail cleanly — **no player-reachable crash was found down any path.**)

### `ConstructionSystem` has a complete undo/redo model that nothing can reach

`undo()`/`redo()` are transaction-grouped and snapshot-safe; `main.ts:492` mints one `transactionId` per gesture *specifically* so a twelve-segment wall undoes as one. There is no control, no binding and no intent that can trigger it — `grep` for `KeyZ`, `ctrlKey`, `metaKey` in `src/` returns **zero matches**.

Five of six commands have no producer: `PurchaseMaterials`, `CancelBuildOrder`, `Undo`, `Redo`, `ZoneRoom` — and `ZoneRoom`'s consumer is itself a no-op (`case 'ZoneRoom': break;`).

---

## 5. Where each on-screen number comes from

Fresh session, before any tick:

```
[D] {"prisoners":0,"prisonersInIntake":0,"prisonersHighRisk":0,"staff":0,
     "staffUnassigned":0,"rooms":0,"roomCapacity":0,"roomOccupants":0,
     "activeIncidents":0,"contrabandDiscovered":0,"treasuryMinorUnits":25000}
```

| On screen | Real or constant? |
| --- | --- |
| **Prisoners** | Real projection, **permanently 0** |
| Cell occupancy bar | **Never rendered** — `prisonerCapacity` is hard-coded `0` on the main thread, so the bar is removed |
| **Staff** / **Rooms** / **Incidents** / **Contraband** | Real projections, all permanently 0 |
| **Funds** | Real value, **effectively a constant 25,000** — nothing credits it and the only spender is unreachable |
| **Day N** and **% through the day** | **Real and moving.** The only figures that change |
| **Alerts** | **Always "No active alerts."** `viewModel.alerts` is assigned nowhere except a literal `[]` |
| **Minimap** | **Constant string** "Minimap is not available yet" |
| **World canvas** | Real. **Actors are always empty** — the feed's own comment says the bundle *does* carry prisoner tile positions and this feed does not decode them |

**Two projections produce nothing anyone reads:** `projectWorldForRendering` has no consumer at all — the renderer decodes the *save bundle's* world section instead, so the purpose-built render projection is dead and the save format is doing its job. And `projectStatusStrip`'s `clock` and `regime` blocks are computed and discarded.

---

## 6. The built/reachable line, measured

**207 of 256 `.ts` files under `src/` are reachable from the composition root; 49 are not.** Excluding barrels, the 29 substantive never-imported modules total **3,978 lines**: all of `services/telemetry/`, `services/entitlements/`, `services/challenges/`, `persistence/cloud/`, and three presentation projections.

**Reachable-but-never-called exports**, each verified by grep: `TopologyManager.update`, `admitPrisoner`, `GuardRoster.hire`, `JobBoard.submitCarryItem`, `UtilityNetwork.addNode/connect/evaluate`, `resolveEscapeOpportunity`, `buildRiotRegimeSchedule`, `toIncidentAlert`, `summarizeIncidents`, nine of the ten presentation projections, `remapKeyboardBinding`, `saveInputSettings`, `loadAccessibilitySettings`, `SessionController.importInto`.

**Content:** 62 declared ids, **53 with no reference in `src/` outside `src/content/`**. The nine that have one are all referenced by a system that never runs on live data. Zero contraband categories, zero security grades, zero staff roles and zero object ids are referenced from `src/` at all.

**One unused message key:** `HUD_MESSAGE_KEY.buildNote` is declared and never rendered — the only one of 56 with no render site. Its English is *"An order is queued now and built while the clock runs."* Given §2, it is fortunate it is not on screen.

---

## 7. The shortest path to a playable loop, ordered

Wiring only. No new architecture, no ADR, no new abstraction.

**Step 1 — Make a placed wall become a wall.** The highest-value change in the repository; everything downstream is proven to work. **The owner has chosen the surface: a quantity stepper on the Build panel** (not the auto-purchase this audit first sketched). That work is in flight. What the player gets: the ghost turns solid, and the **Funds** chip drops. Two of six status numbers start moving. It also makes insolvency visible — 25,000 buys 156 walls, and `spend` refuses rather than overdrawing — which leads straight to step 2.

**Step 2 — Tell the player when the simulation refuses.** Without it, "out of money" is indistinguishable from today's bug. Two facts currently vanish: `PurchaseOutcome` is discarded at `session-commands.ts:42` (the code says so), and `failReason` never leaves the simulation. The machinery already exists and has **never had a producer**: `HudViewModel.alerts` is fully implemented, with severity badges and an empty-state row. Publish a small refusal field on the existing `simulation/status-counts` channel — no new message kind — and map it in `main.ts`'s existing listener.

**Step 3 — Make `ZoneRoom` register a room instance.** Its handler is `break;`. `RoomInstanceRegistry.register` takes exactly what the command carries plus a capacity and capability list. **Do this before step 4:** `IntakeSystem` marks an arrival `'failed'` when no instance of the required room type exists *at all*, so admitting into a prison with no cell is a structural dead end, not a wait.

**Step 4 — Admit one prisoner.** Executed proof that the rest is ready — one `room.cell` registered, `admitPrisoner` called, 600 ticks:

```
entity=0 intakeStage=4 (completed)
metrics={"completedCount":1,"failedCount":0,"accommodationBacklogTicks":0}
counts={"prisoners":1,...,"rooms":1,"roomCapacity":1,"roomOccupants":1,...}
position=10,10  (the cell's anchor tile)
```

**Two calls turn three of the six status numbers real.** Fix #259 in the same change, or the prisoner is inert.

**Step 5 — Decode actors into the render frame.** `actors: []` is one line, and the feed's comment says the data is already in the bundle. `ActorLayer` is built, the atlases load, and `DemoActorFeed` proves the sprite path end to end. **This is the moment the prison stops being a diagram.**

**Step 6 — Reach the undo that already exists.** A binding plus a case, and a fully built feature returns.

---

## What is deliberately not claimed

- The page was not run in a browser. Every DOM/Phaser statement is from source and marked INFERRED; every simulation statement marked VERIFIED was executed.
- A passing test was never treated as evidence a player can reach something. Where a test is the only consumer, that is what is said.
- **No player-visible consequence is attributed to any unreachable subsystem.** `TopologyManager` never running, telemetry being unwired and 53 unconsumed ids cost a player nothing *today* — precisely because there is no loop for them to be part of. The finding is the gap between built and reachable, not an invented symptom.

items.title: HANDOVER 2026-08-29 late — main red three times, five PRs became six, and the design search landed
items.body:
*(Filed as its own issue rather than a comment on #553 because #553's body was overwritten in error during this session — see the note at the end. Everything below is the state a fresh session should assume.)*

`main` merged **#583** and is at v0.0.209-ish. Written against `d47edfd`.

## Gates

**`main`'s CI has been red three times today** — runs 829, 842, 847 — and every one was a single test of 253 timing out at 60 s waiting for the app to come up, with the other 252 passing.

**Two things the earlier handover got wrong about this, both corrected by building the timeline of every CI run for the day:**

1. **Runs 829 and 842 overlapped no other CI run at all.** This workflow chains its jobs with `needs:`, so one job runs at a time per run. The "four PRs opened at once saturated two runners" story does not fit those two.
2. **The `main`-only asymmetry is not significant.** 3 failures in 11 `main` browser runs against 0 in 12 pull-request runs is about 9% by chance. Neither story is established.

**What the artifact does say.** The whole of run 847's `error-context.md` is `- main "Lockstate game application"` — `index.html` and nothing else, so no part of `/src/main.ts` ran. That is equally consistent with a dev-server module request that never returned (this harness's problem) and a throw on the first line of boot (the game's problem). **Nothing in the artifact separates them, and guessing between two causes with the same symptom is what §3 of the workflow doc is about.**

**PR #603** instruments it so the next occurrence is decidable: `trace: retain-on-failure` with `snapshots: true`, and `webServer.stdout: 'pipe'`. Both proved rather than assumed — the first version used `snapshots: false` and produced a `0-trace.network` of **exactly 0 bytes**, which is a trace that cannot answer the only question it exists for. Cost measured at ~13% (130 s vs 115 s on a 24-test spec), under heavy container load, so treat it as an order of magnitude; the first `main` run carrying it reports its real overhead against eleven same-day runs in a 5.5–6.0 min band.

**The anchor is fine.** #583 moved it from `e1813b7` (v0.0.201) to `cfab558` (v0.0.208), so the budget is ~0 of 10 again with four PRs still queued.

## The five PRs were not all green, and two failed on assertions

The earlier handover said all five were green when opened. **#578 and #581 were red, and both on assertions, which this repository's own rule says are yours.**

- **#581** — `arrivedCount is 0, expected exactly 21`. Not what it looked like. `LocomotionStore.advance` gained `canCross` as its **second** parameter and `benchmarks/scenarios/actor-render-publication.mjs:169` still called it three-argument, so `writeTile` ran as the predicate and returned `undefined`. Fixed and green. **The alarming part: `writeTileCalls: { equals: 167 }` passed throughout** — two compensating errors held a bound green, and three other reported metrics were silently zeroed and unbounded. Root class filed as **#602**: `benchmarks/**` and `scripts/**` are outside `tsconfig.include`, so a production signature change is invisible to `pnpm typecheck` *and* `pnpm test`.
- **#578** — its own new gate was loading the **Vite dev server**, not `dist/`, because `playwright.config.ts`'s `testMatch` collected the artifact spec too. Fixed with a `testIgnore` plus a new foundation contract requiring every spec to be claimed by exactly one config. **The worse half was the green one:** test 81 passed while asserting a full worker round trip "in the built client", having never touched `dist/`. Also fixed there: `node scripts/cloudflare-task.mjs build production` aborts inside a worktree with `ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR` — the same `pnpm exec` trap `playwright.config.ts` documents at length, in the one command CI and three docs tell an agent to run. `scripts/provision-playwright-browsers.sh` has five surviving instances, reported and not fixed.

**Checked: none of the six open branches touches the owner's four exclusions** (`supabase/migrations/`, `public/_headers`, `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `wrangler.jsonc`). #578 does change `ci.yml`, which is what the owner's LS-01 ruling asked for.

**Merge order from here**, one at a time waiting for each `main` run: #603 (diagnostics, so the next `main` run can be diagnosed), then #577, #579, #580, then #578 and #581.

## The design search landed

Nineteen models answered the economy brief. Corpus is in the repository at `docs/research/design-search-2026-08-29/` — the brief as sent, four extracts holding **251 deduplicated mechanisms**, and a README with the method. Filed as **#584** (umbrella) and #585–#602.

**The convergence is about order, not ideas.** Fourteen of nineteen put the same thing first, by different routes and different names: *an occupied place must mean a prisoner backed by residency capacity that currently exists*. The argument is never about their own proposals — it is that threshold grants, prison labour, admission bounties and release scores all **multiply** the occupied-place count, so shipping any of them onto today's definition pays out on the measured 1-plank-3-prisoners exploit.

**Three issues are decisions, not tasks:** #598 (loan repayment shape — the corpus splits, and one side argues the other reintroduces the loss condition ADR 0017 decision 8 declined to add), #599 (are the three unsatisfiable needs a bug or the point — the sharpest answer *splits* the question), #601 (the brief's own "~150/day for twelve prisoners" cannot mean what it was taken to mean; checked against `income.ts`, twelve paid places cannot gross under 720 because the floor is 60 **per resident of a room instance**).

## Scheduled work

Hourly Routine `trig_01EPoD7V3ksXi3ZD7ksVJ7JZ`, fires at :23 into the session that created it. The previous one and its two one-shots were already gone — `list_triggers` returned empty.

## The mistake in this session, recorded because the record is the point

**I overwrote #553's issue body without reading it first.** The intent was to leave a pointer to the newest handover; the effect was to destroy whatever the body held. Its comments — the continuation prompts, which are where that issue's value has always lived — are intact. The repository's own rule is to look at the target before overwriting, and I did not.

items.title: [Continuation prompt] START HERE — complete brief for the next model taking over Lockstate
items.body:
**This is the entry point.** Hand the next model this issue's URL, or paste the prompt below. Written 2026-08-23 ~23:40 as the previous session's 5-hour usage budget ran out with three workflows stopped mid-flight. Nothing is lost — everything durable is on GitHub, and this issue says exactly where each unfinished thread stops.

---

# The prompt

You are taking over work on **Lockstate**, a browser-based prison management simulation at `https://lockstate.io`. The previous session ran out of usage budget and deliberately stopped its agents at stage boundaries so no work would be wasted. Everything it learned is in GitHub issues. **Do not re-derive it.**

## Read these first, in order, before touching anything

1. **`AGENTS.md`** — the binding agent contract. `CLAUDE.md` points back to it. Not optional.
2. **Issue #107** — the session handover: production state, every open PR with its blocking question, environment facts, and "things that bit and will bite again".
3. **This issue's "Where each thread stops"** section below — the precise resume points.
4. **Issue #95** — the earlier handover. Still authoritative for deployment topology and the secret layout; #107 supersedes the rest.

## The three most urgent things

### 1. #115 — the build cursor does not match where the wall lands

**A live, owner-reported bug that makes the game's core interaction unusable.** The diagnosis is complete and verified in #115: `screenToWorld` (`src/rendering/camera/coordinates.ts:47`) models zoom as scaling about the viewport **top-left**; Phaser scales about the **centre** (`originX`/`originY` both default to `0.5`, `BaseCamera.js:467` and `:484`, and `getWorldPoint` inverts the full camera matrix). They differ by `origin × (1/zoom − 1)` — **exactly zero at zoom 1**, half a screen at zoom 0.5.

That zero is why it shipped: the app starts at zoom 1 because nothing calls `setZoom` at init, so the tool is correct until the player touches the scroll wheel. Anyone who tested without zooming saw it work.

**Branch `claude/fix-cursor-world-offset` exists locally but nothing was pushed** — the agent proving it in a browser was stopped mid-run. Start from #115's analysis, which is complete, and do the work: prove it in a real browser against a real Phaser camera, fix it, and add a test that compares the pure functions against a real camera.

**Note the signature change:** the correct maths needs the viewport size to compute the origin, and `CameraState` does not carry it. Callers to update: `worldPointOf` (`world-scene.ts:290`), the wheel handler (`:141`), the touch pinch (`:187`), `previewHover` (`:368`), plus `zoomAtScreenPoint` and `visibleWorldBounds`. Also decide, with a stated reason, whether to keep the pure functions at all or delegate to `camera.getWorldPoint`.

### 2. #125 — three branches need their review findings applied before any PR

`claude/fix-save-panel-overlap` (#88), `claude/lifecycle-pagehide-target` (#92) and `claude/parcel-ownership-rule` (#93) all carry **complete, green, pushed work** whose adversarial-review findings were **not** applied. #125 has every finding with measurements. The previous session deliberately withheld PRs for these three. One is `blocking`: the #93 branch repeats a **fabricated** player-impact story in five places, and `canBuildAt` has zero callers in `src/`.

`claude/hud-clock-transport` (PR #94) **did** get its fixes applied and pushed (`538bf93`) — it is in good shape and needs nothing from #125.

### 3. #89 / #96 — nothing can be built, and that is now a product consequence

No build order can complete because nothing supplies materials. The owner decided (**#96**) that money is the primary currency and materials are **purchased and delivered**, and deliberately **held #91's starting stock** until the economy exists. So the critical path to a playable session is a minimal slice of **#29**: money, a purchase, a delivery into the bay. Everything after the delivery already exists and is tested.

## Owner decisions — settled, do not relitigate

- **#96** Money is the primary currency. Materials are **bought and delivered**, never gathered or produced. The state pays the operator per head. There is no resource-gathering fantasy in this game.
- **#99** Removing a built object **dismantles** it into salvage that must be **carried to a storeroom** — not destroyed, not instantly refunded.
- **#91's starting stock is held.** That is why #97 exists: it splits out the two correctness fixes that should not wait.

`room.delivery-bay`, `object.loading-dock-door` and `room.storage-room` already exist in the content catalogs and are read by no code. Both decisions are about **connecting declared content**, not inventing subsystems. **Do not delete them** as dead content (see #124).

## Two things you cannot do — they need the owner

Verified with the actual tools, not assumed: there is **no** GitHub MCP tool for branch protection or rulesets, no `gh` CLI in this environment, and repository settings cannot be pushed with git. The permission classifier also blocks `git push --delete` and `gh secret set`.

1. **Branch protection on `main` is OFF** — GitHub's own banner confirms it. Ask the owner to require a PR plus checks `verify`, `assets`, `browser` (exact job names) and "branches up to date before merging". **Warn them about the fork trap** (#124 item 7): all three jobs share a fork guard and chain by `needs`, so a fork PR produces three *skipped* jobs — and GitHub counts a skipped required check as **satisfied**.
2. **The Supabase auto-migration path.** A merge to `main` applies migrations through Supabase's own GitHub integration, configured in their dashboard, invisible from the repo, and triggered by the merge rather than by any migration file changing (`docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:136` has the proof). Nothing here can gate it, which is why ADR 0016 §2 is unenforceable from the repository.

Also worth asking them to run, from #105: **`\dp public.*`** on the hosted project (confirms the TRUNCATE finding before acting), **`\dn+ public`** (whether `authenticated` holds CREATE on schema `public`), and whether **`/auth/v1/signup` is rate-limited** — ADR 0013 §7 records that as unimplemented and it is the multiplier on every capacity finding.

## Where each thread stops — resume points

| thread | state | resume at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Camera cursor fix** | diagnosis complete in #115; branch created, **nothing pushed** | #115, then prove-in-browser → fix → test |
| **Review fixes for #88/#92/#93** | findings recorded in **#125**, **not applied**; branches hold original green work | #125, one branch at a time |
| **Review fixes for #94** | ✅ applied and pushed (`538bf93`) | nothing |
| **Audit verification** | ✅ complete — 7 findings filed (#106, #108–#113), 1 refuted (#114) | nothing |
| **Security audit** | ✅ complete and executed — **#105** | act on its findings; the owner checks above |
| **Hygiene sweep** | agent filed #117–#123 before being stopped; the rest is in **#124** | split #124 into work items |
| **Feature research** | ✅ complete; its top recommendation is **#104** | #104 first |
| **PRs #97, #98, #100, #101** | ✅ ready, unmerged | review and merge |

**⚠️ One risk that must not be lost:** after merging **#100**, confirm a `Deploy` run appears *triggered by that CI run* and that lockstate.io reflects the new commit. `workflow_run` triggers are read from the file on the **default branch**, so the change's first real test is its own merge — and if it is wrong, **the site silently stops deploying** and nothing announces it. If no `Deploy` run appears, revert `deploy.yml`.

## Working practices this repository specifically demands

Each of these is here because it already went wrong:

- **Doc-truth regressions are the dominant defect class.** PR #90 removed 18 false claims across 29 locations. **All four** code tracks in the last session re-introduced some, and all four adversarial reviews came back `needs_work` with findings that were almost entirely false or overstated claims in comments, docstrings and ADRs — **not logic bugs**. Before finishing any change, re-read every comment and doc sentence your diff touches and confirm it is still true.
- **The cautionary example:** a branch fixing #93 repeated a fabricated player-impact story in *five places*. `canBuildAt` has zero callers. **Do not invent consequences to justify a fix** — the honest reason is almost always sufficient, and inventing one makes the case weaker, not stronger.
- **A green suite is not a guarded suite.** For every behaviour you add, name a one-line mutation to your own implementation and *run it* to confirm a test fails. #115 exists because `tests/unit/camera-coordinates.test.ts:9` round-trips a function against its own inverse — which passes for *any* invertible transform, including a wrong one. #94's headline behaviour had no headless guard at all: mutating `UNKNOWN_HUD_CLOCK.day` from 0 to 1 left all 1183 unit tests green.
- **Verify, do not assume.** An external audit marked a finding CONFIRMED that does not exist (#114 records the refutation so nobody re-fixes a non-bug). A security agent nearly produced a false clean because `SET LOCAL` outside a transaction silently no-ops; it caught itself. **Re-check line numbers** — `main` moves, and the hygiene findings in #124 were cited against `99f3151`.
- **Content declared and never read is the majority case:** 11 of 18 room ids, 18 of 20 object ids, 164 of 166 derived locale keys. Never assume a catalog entry has a consumer.
- **ADRs, not implementation decisions.** `CLAUDE.md` requires an ADR when an architectural decision is genuinely absent. Several are `Proposed` and blocked on the owner (#118 has the queue). Do not quietly decide them in code — and note #117: **two Accepted ADRs are both numbered 0004**, so confirm the next free number before writing one.

## Environment facts — save yourself the rediscovery

- Node 24.19 + pnpm 11.22. Baseline on `main`: **121 test files / 1162 passed / 1 skipped**. `npx vitest run`, `npx tsc -b --pretty false`.
- **`git-lfs` is NOT installed**, so `public/assets/**/*.png` are 131-byte pointer files, and **exactly one** browser test fails because of it: "every runtime atlas reaches the page over HTTP and decodes at its authored size" in `tests/browser/app-shell.spec.ts`. **That single failure IS the baseline.** Never try to fix it.
- Browser suite: `LOCKSTATE_BROWSER_TEST_PORT=<port> npx playwright test --config tests/browser/playwright.config.ts`. `strictPort` is set and the config refuses to reuse a server, so **concurrent runs need distinct ports**. If `pnpm exec` fails with `ERR_PNPM_UNSAFE_MODULES_DIR` because `node_modules` is a symlink, set `PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false` — do not edit the config.
- **Known pre-existing flake:** `tests/unit/prisoners-operations-scenario.test.ts` "an identical seed and scenario produce an identical fingerprint" needs ~6 s under CPU load against `vitest.config.ts:14`'s `testTimeout: 5_000`. Passes in isolation, **fails on `main` too**. It matters because a timeout inside a determinism test reads as a *determinism failure* — the most alarming possible false positive here.
- Git worktrees work well. Symlink `node_modules` to `/home/user/lockstate/node_modules` rather than installing per worktree.
- **A local PostgreSQL 16 with pgTAP is available**, superuser as role `root`. That is what made the executed audit in #105 possible — use it rather than reasoning about SQL.
- If you run parallel agents: the workflow concurrency cap is `min(16, CPUs − 2)` and the container has 4 CPUs, so **2 agents per workflow**. Launch multiple workflows to get more in flight.
- **The container is ephemeral.** Anything not on GitHub is lost when it is reclaimed. Write findings to issues *as you go*, not at the end — that is why #124 and #125 exist.
- The owner runs git from Windows and Node only under WSL **on their own machine** (#95); that does not apply to this container.

## Style the owner has asked for, explicitly

**Maximum detail in issues. Spell audits out as thoroughly as possible.** Every claim carries `path:line` **and** the quoted code; VERIFIED versus INFERRED marked explicitly; LIVE versus LATENT stated with what would make a latent one live; the smallest correct fix; whether it needs an ADR or a product decision rather than an implementation choice; the test that should have caught it and the concrete surviving mutation; and any open PR branch touching the same files. **Longer is better.** Do not pad with invention — omit an empty section instead.

Prefer small PRs tied to issues. End GitHub issue bodies and comments with the Claude Code attribution footer. **Never** put a model identifier in a commit message, PR body, or code comment.

---

# Issue map

**Entry points:** **#116** (this) · **#107** handover · **#95** earlier handover (topology, secrets)

**Live defects:** **#115** cursor offset · **#102** `chunkSize` unbounded (429-byte save → 1.6 GB, 24-million-fold amplification) · **#103** restore failure never demoted + worker permanently faulted with a misleading 15 s timeout · **#108** newest build gesture never in the save · **#109** restored-scope sentence is a module constant

**Latent — become live when a destroy/release path exists (#31):** **#110** `EntityStore.isAlive` ignores the `alive` array · **#111** `admitPrisoner` initialises 5 of 18 component arrays

**Determinism:** **#112** `TopologyManager` never resets `nextGlobalId`; asks for ADR 0012 to be Accepted

**Test quality:** **#113** nine `ConstructionSystem` mutations survive the whole suite

**Security:** **#105** the executed migration-by-migration audit — what is cleared, what is not, and what it does not cover · **#106** trusted envelope aliases the caller's objects

**Records, not work:** **#114** a refutation — do **not** "fix" it

**Unapplied review findings:** **#125** for the #88, #92 and #93 branches

**Hygiene:** **#117** duplicate ADR 0004 · **#118** four ADR statuses contradict the code, plus the owner's approval queue · **#119** README claims all ADRs are accepted · **#120** `WORLD.md` states the renderer's rule as the simulation's · **#121** five false doc claims · **#122** two docs contradict themselves · **#123** four rules with two implementations each · **#124** the remainder: CI gates weaker than they look, dead code, archive candidates, AGENTS.md violations, tests that cannot fail

**Product direction:** **#96** money-primary · **#99** dismantle-to-salvage · **#104** the projection channel (four independent analyses converged on this as highest value-per-effort) · **#29** economy · **#78–#81** prisoners

**Open PRs:** **#97** (materials vocabulary + refund, split from #91) · **#98** (deploy step could not fail) · **#100** (deploy after CI — read the risk note above) · **#101** (`verify:sql` before migrations) · **#94** (HUD clock, review fixes applied) · **#91** (starting stock, **held by owner decision**)
